steps.title: Today's market compass overview
steps.narration: The homepage shows today's market state at a glance. You see the key metrics, what changed since yesterday, and next-session focus candidates stacked in a natural reading order.
steps.point_out: The page displays the market-state band at top, the plain-English summary, a 'What changed' card comparing to the prior session, Leadership rotation, next-session candidates with their reasoning, and the frozen manifest strip at the bottom.

steps.title: Incident recovery: August 12th data serves cleanly
steps.narration: August 12th was one of two dates deleted by an earlier data incident. Viewing this historical date now shows it has been recovered and renders without error.
steps.point_out: The page loads cleanly showing 2026-08-12's market state in the tiles. The manifest strip at the bottom shows the basis as 'available' or 'rebuilt'—confirming this date is accessible again.

steps.title: Incident recovery: August 5th renders with honest basis state
steps.narration: August 5th is another incident date whose manifest was previously orphaned. Viewing it now shows the page renders and displays an honest state about the data basis.
steps.point_out: The manifest strip shows the correct basis state for this date—either 'available' if the underlying data was recovered, or an honest 'unknown' if the source remains unverified. There is no false claim.

steps.title: Return to today's view
steps.narration: We navigate back to the latest data to explore how the system explains its reasoning and data sources.
steps.point_out: The home page is now showing today's market state and focus candidates.

steps.title: Summary backs every statement with cited data
steps.narration: The summary card explains the market state. When you expand it, every sentence shows which template it used and the exact data values that generated it.
steps.point_out: Click 'Show cited facts' to reveal that each summary statement lists its template ID and the specific values (breadth counts, threshold levels, metrics) the system cited to generate that sentence. This shows the system does not invent reasoning.

steps.title: Market analysis tools show regime and breadth detail
steps.narration: The market page houses tools too detailed for the homepage. Here you see the regime × market-phase cross-view chart and deeper breadth analysis.
steps.point_out: You'll see the regime × phase cross-view chart, glance tiles, three breadth breakdown cards, Top Sectors and Top Themes, Candidate Counts, and the full Market Phase & Severity breakdown—all the market-analysis tools in one comprehensive view.

steps.title: Sector attribution is honest and near-complete
steps.narration: The stocks page lists every stock with its assigned sector. Sectors come from a two-source method: first a curated config, then a fallback for unmapped symbols.
steps.point_out: Select 'Unassigned' in the Sector filter. The unassigned count should be at most 5% of total members—never the old baseline of 78%. This shows the two-source attribution is working correctly.

steps.title: Methodology page explains data sources and scope
steps.narration: The methodology page discloses how the system works. It explains the two-source sector approach and clarifies that sector history is current-only—there is no point-in-time historical data.
steps.point_out: The Universe/Data section lists both the curated config and pool-snapshot sources, and explicitly states sector assignments apply only to the current session. This transparency helps you understand what the data does and does not cover.
